Priya to share recent benchmark spreadsheet (p50/p95 latency) and quantization notes

summary: Renewal check-in focusing on expanding Dedicated capacity to 4x GPUs, enabling two additional regions (eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1), and discussing contract extension options and procurement timing. Customer wants performance numbers, cost impact, and a potential on-prem pilot for sensitive workloads.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood — we scheduled 60 minutes to go over renewal and expansion needs. quick roll call?
[00:08] Tom Reyes: Tom here, head of platform at Mariner.
[00:11] Aisha Khan: Aisha, CTO.
[00:13] Ben Ortega: Ben — procurement.
[00:16] Priya Gupta: Priya, solutions engineer at Redwood.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: cool, thanks. so high level — you're up for renewal in june and mentioned wanting more capacity and regions, is that right?
[00:29] Tom Reyes: yeah, correct. we've tripled usage since last quarter, um the current Dedicated pool runs out of headroom during peak routing windows, p95 latency spikes and that's hurting UX.
[00:41] Aisha Khan: plus we need two more regions — eu-west and ap-southeast — for latency and data residency for a couple of customers.
[00:49] Jordan Lee: got it, makes sense. Priya, do you want to summarize the Dedicated upgrade options?
[00:54] Priya Gupta: sure. currently you're on a 2x-gpu dedicated pool with burst. we recommend moving to a 4x-gpu reserved pool which gives roughly 2.8x throughput depending on batching and KV cache hit rate. you can also enable cross-region replication for model artifacts. note there is a cost delta and a different SLA tier.
[01:12] Ben Ortega: cost is the big one for procurement — can you give rough numbers now?
[01:16] Jordan Lee: rough ballpark, upgrading to 4x Dedicated increases committed monthly by about 2.2x — i'll send exact pricing; there are discounts for annual commits. also we can show cost per 1M tokens with quantized models and batching applied.
[01:28] Tom Reyes: okay, and what about latency targets? we need p95 under 350ms for chat flows. last week we saw p95 around 480ms during peaks.
[01:37] Priya Gupta: correct, that aligns with what our logs showed. with 4x plus tuned batching and prefix caching you'll typically see p95 drop into the 300–350ms range for the same model and payload. we'll share the benchmark sheet.
[01:50] Aisha Khan: what about dedicated in eu-west and ap-southeast? can you host Dedicated there or is that only Hosted?
[01:56] Jordan Lee: we support Dedicated in those regions — there are capacity lead times for certain GPU types. Priya, region availability note?
[02:02] Priya Gupta: eu-west-1 is available immediately for the q8b/rtx-class pools; ap-southeast-1 has limited availability for q8b — lead time ~3–4 weeks unless you take a different SKU. we can propose a staged rollout — start eu-west, then ap-southeast.
[02:20] Ben Ortega: and for data residency, we need logs and models to stay in eu for EU customers. is that supported?
[02:26] Jordan Lee: yes — we have data locality controls and the Private offering for full control. for Hosted/Dedicated we can ensure storage and logs are kept in-region and provide audit logs. for stricter requirements, the Private VPC deployment or on-prem is available.
[02:40] Aisha Khan: about Private/on-prem — we have one customer that needs air-gapped processing for certain docs. what would that look like as a pilot?
[02:47] Priya Gupta: typically a pilot is a short on-prem appliance or VPC instance for the sensitive workload. it requires procurement lead time and an onboarding checklist — KMS integration, SOC2 checklist, network tunnels. Jordan will coordinate procurement docs.
[03:02] Tom Reyes: procurement timeline — Ben, can you speak?
[03:04] Ben Ortega: we usually need 2–3 weeks to review contract changes, then legal takes 1–2 weeks. if pricing matches our budget we'll move quickly.
[03:11] Jordan Lee: great — so action items: we'll send pricing, benchmarks, and the security checklist. any outstanding technical blockers?
[03:18] Tom Reyes: one: model variants. we rely on a fine-tuned model. will that be supported in Dedicated?
[03:24] Priya Gupta: yes, you can pin model versions and we support custom artifacts. if you need quantization we'll test the specific variant to check quality regression.
[03:33] Aisha Khan: regression testing is important — can you run a small eval set?
[03:36] Priya Gupta: absolutely, send us a red-team prompt set or the evals and we'll run A/B with quantized vs fp16 and share quality metrics.
[03:45] Tom Reyes: another concern: failover. if a region goes down, can traffic failover to another region with low impact?
[03:52] Jordan Lee: yes, smart routing can fall back to alternative regions or model variants; there's a small latency penalty but better than errors. there are config options to control which workloads can cross-region.
[04:03] Ben Ortega: for procurement we need contract term options — 12 vs 36 months, and an SLA credit table.
[04:10] Jordan Lee: we can provide 12/24/36 month pricing tiers, and SLA-backed credits. i'll attach the contract addendum with options.
[04:18] Aisha Khan: any known competitors offering better region coverage? we briefly evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI — how does Redwood compare for cost at scale?
[04:26] Priya Gupta: in benchmarks we typically show Redwood offering competitive per-token cost when Dedicated + quantization are used; many customers find we win on predictable throughput and observability. i'll include a comparative slide.
[04:37] Tom Reyes: great. timeline — we want to finalize by end of april to get Dedicated capacity in place before peak season in june.
[04:44] Jordan Lee: that should be doable. Jordan to send pricing by 03/24, Priya benchmarks 03/23, customer to confirm regions by 03/29 — we can reconvene after those items.
[04:55] Ben Ortega: one more procurement note: please include PO terms and a standard reachback for support contacts.
[04:59] Jordan Lee: will do. anything else?
[05:02] Aisha Khan: no, that covers it. thanks.
[05:05] Jordan Lee: ok thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and a proposed contract. meeting adjourned.

Note: transcription contains a few word substitutions (e.g., q8b references and GPU SKUs may be abbreviated). Timestamps are approximate and inserted every 30–60s.
